## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)
- [`sat26-sparse`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-sparse)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(n(\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Retain every vertex, including isolated vertices, which belong to every maximal independent set. For n = 0, the empty set is the unique maximal independent set and unique minimal vertex cover; handle invalid requested sizes directly.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O(n)$ |
| Clauses | $O(n+m)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $3$ |

## Derivation

1. Use selection bits x_v and impose $\neg x_u\vee\neg x_v$ for every edge uv, so the selected set S is independent. It is maximal exactly when it also dominates every vertex: an undominated vertex could be added, and a dominated unselected vertex cannot be added.

2. Add optional markers y_v and all clauses $\neg y_v\vee\neg x_u$ for u∈N[v]. Compute the marker parity with n−1 binary XOR gates and full equivalences when n≥1. Let H_0 and H_1 additionally require even and odd parity, respectively. An independent S contributes $\sum_{T\subseteq U(S)}(-1)^{|T|}$ to $\#H_0-\#H_1$, so precisely the maximal independent sets remain. Here U(S) is the set of vertices undominated by S.

3. Both formulas have 2n selection/marker bits, at most n−1 XOR outputs, and O(n) extra variables if $\sum_v x_v=r$ is requested. Full XOR and cardinality equivalences uniquely determine every gate output for fixed x and y. The m independence clauses, n+2m marker clauses, parity clauses, and optional cardinality clauses give N=O(n), M=O(n+m), and width at most three.

4. Two sequential exact #SAT calls and subtraction give A(n)L^{O(1)} time and polynomial space. Each parity count is at most 2^(2n), with O(n) bits, and an explicit CNF has bit length O((n+m) log(n+2)), polynomial in L. The separately reported formalization profile uses its own weaker exponent. If m≤Dn for fixed D, the sparse assumption, with forced-zero padding if needed, also yields B(n)L^{O(1)}.

5. Complementation is a bijection: S is a maximal independent set exactly when V∖S is an inclusion-minimal vertex cover. Hence the same total count applies to minimal vertex covers; minimal covers of size r correspond to maximal independent sets of size n−r. This correspondence preserves the count without a multiplicity correction.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- This counts inclusion-maximal independent sets and inclusion-minimal vertex covers. It is different from counting maximum independent sets or minimum vertex covers.
- The reduction uses the full exact-counting assumption. Markers are optional witnesses of being undominated; they are canceled by the even-minus-odd difference, so counting only one parity formula gives a different quantity.
- The result is a counting algorithm, not an algorithm enumerating every set within the same total time. No weighted extension, novelty claim, or latest-best comparison is asserted.

Counting requires a count-preserving encoding and preprocessing, or an explicit correction for multiplicities. The derivation must justify this; decision preservation alone is insufficient.
